title: Stage-aware KV micro-partitioning to reduce cross-stage synchronization
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem:
Continuous batching combined with tensor/pipeline parallel execution leads to large numbers of in-flight KV partitions being materialized across GPUs. Each pipeline stage currently holds conservative KV slices which causes peak memory amplification when request batches overlap multiple sequence lengths and many concurrent requests are routed through different pipeline stages. Cross-stage synchronization (coarse locks or synchronous RPCs) to ensure consistent K/V access increases tail latency and reduces throughput during bursty workloads.

Goals:
- Reduce peak per-GPU KV memory by introducing stage-aware micro-partitioning so each pipeline stage only materializes the minimum required KV slices for the requests it executes.
- Minimize cross-stage synchronization and avoid global locks during continuous batching.
- Maintain or improve P95/P99 latency and overall throughput under representative production mixes.
- Provide graceful fallback to global spill tiers when memory budgets are exhausted.

Proposal (high level):
1) Micro-partitioning: split KV cache by (model, prefix-hash, pipeline-stage) micro-shards. Ownership is stage-affine: during planning, requests are assigned preferred micro-shards for the pipeline stages they will traverse. Micro-shards are small (configurable shard-size) to allow fine-grained allocation and migration.

2) Lightweight ownership metadata: each micro-shard has an epoch counter and ownership token (owner stage id). Updates are applied to per-stage shadow logs and merged to the authoritative micro-shard on a low-latency background thread. Readers in a stage consult the local shadow first, then the authoritative shard; no cross-stage blocking required for nominal reads.

3) Prefetch + eviction hints: batching scheduler emits per-request prefetch hints targeted to the assigned stage micro-shards to warm KV before the stage executes. Eviction uses a two-tier policy: stage-local LRU for micro-shard candidates + global pressure-driven compaction where contiguous micro-shards are spilled to host memory.

4) Epoch barriers vs locks: use lightweight epoch barriers to ensure correctness at the boundary of a dynamic micro-shard re-assignment (e.g., when autoscaler moves a stage or when a micro-shard is reparented). This avoids expensive global locks.

5) Per-stage memory budgets and admission control: offer configurable soft budgets per stage (based on throughput and SLO tier). Admission controller will trigger early fallback rules (lower-precision variant, compacted KV entries, or spill) when soft budget crossed.

6) Monitoring and metrics: expose per-micro-shard memory, local-hit-rate, inter-stage read-misses, prefetch success ratio, epoch-stall-count, and spill rate. Build a dashboard and release regression alerts if memory headroom decreases by >15% or P99 latency increases >10%.

Trade-offs considered:
- Increased metadata and bookkeeping vs memory savings: micro-shard metadata adds overhead but is expected to be <3% of baseline KV footprint for typical shard sizes.
- Slight write amplification from shadow log merges vs avoiding synchronous inter-stage RPCs. We expect merges to be amortized and dominated by read traffic patterns.
- Complexity of reparenting shards across autoscaling events vs preserving low-latency reads; reparenting will be staged via epoch barriers to bound interruption.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Spike (done): simulator that models per-stage request trajectories, estimated memory footprint reduction with shard sizes {4KB, 16KB, 64KB}. Preliminary sim shows median peak memory reduction ~28% at 16KB shard size for production mix.
- Design doc (this ticket): finalize APIs, shard sizing defaults, metrics, and safety nets.
- Runtime changes: allocator changes (per-stage arenas), micro-partition manager, shadow-log implementation, background merger, prefetch hint plumbing in batching scheduler.
- Tests & harness: unit tests for epoch barrier correctness, integration load tests with continuous batching harness, fault-injection tests for reparenting.
- Canary rollout: enable per-customer opt-in with detailed metrics and automatic rollback on SLO regressions.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end P95/P99 latency under canary load does not regress by >5% vs baseline.
- Peak GPU KV memory reduced by >=25% in canary runs for target workload mix.
- No data-corruption incidents in shadow merge scenarios (validated by unit+integration tests).
- Telemetry: per-shard metrics published, and a dashboard created showing memory headroom and prefetch effectiveness.
- Documentation for on-call runbook for canary rollback.

Benchmarks & success metrics to collect:
- Peak per-GPU KV memory (MB) and 95th percentile across hosts
- Continuous batching throughput (req/s) and token/s
- Prefetch hit ratio and latency delta on prefetched keys
- Inter-stage read miss rate and merge overhead (CPU%)
- Failure/reparenting time (ms) during autoscaler events

Rollout strategy:
- Internal load-test cluster (nightly) -> limited canary customers (20% traffic) -> wider canary (50%) -> GA.
- Default configuration will be conservative (higher shard size) and per-customer tuning will be possible.
